title: M6 runtime: 50 random power cuts
description: Including cuts during pairing and while saving settings: the device always boots and `config.json`/`session.db` stay valid (no re-pairing).

title: M6 runtime: watchdog test
description: `kill -STOP` the binary → the device reboots within 60 s and comes back.

title: M6 runtime: M5b scenarios pass on both images
description: Repeat the M5b scenarios on the flashed images, not just on the distro.

title: M6 runtime: boot to the web UI < 30 s (Pi 2) / < 45 s (BBB)
description: Flash both cards, measure from power-on to the UI answering on the network.

title: M6 runtime: RAM budget on both boards
description: wa-transcriber RSS < 60 MB and the whole system < 100 MB used, with ≥ 30 MB free on the 512 MB BBB.

title: M5b: record dongles and results in docs/hardware.md
description: Board, distro, dongle chipset/driver, pass/fail per scenario per board, and any deviation from the design; then update docs/STATUS.md.

title: M5b: eight scenarios on the Raspberry Pi 2
description: Binary in managed mode as a systemd service, each scenario 3×: setup AP + captive portal, join home WiFi, wrong passphrase, router off/on, ethernet and link-local, `!reset`, 24 h soak. Full list: docs/PLAN.md#m5b exit criteria.

title: M5b: eight scenarios on the Cubieboard
description: Same scenarios, same 3× repetition, on the Allwinner A10 board with onboard ethernet plus a dongle.

title: M5b: dongle AP-mode gate on both boards
description: On the Pi 2 (Raspberry Pi OS Lite) and the Cubieboard (Debian/Armbian): record `lsusb`, `iw list` supported interface modes and the driver. Pass if AP is listed and a 10-minute manual hostapd test lets a phone connect; else buy an RT5370 or MT7612U and repeat.

title: M2: write the decision (claim vs tag) and retire the experiment code
description: Apply the decision table at the end of docs/PLAN.md#m2, write it into M2-results.md, then either delete the experiment code or keep it behind `WAT_EXPERIMENTS` and document why.

title: M2: run the probe matrix on real phones and write docs/experiments/M2-results.md
description: Owner, needs two accounts. Run each variant 10× in the A–B private chat and 10× in a group with a third person; record every client of A and B (Android, iPhone, WhatsApp Web, desktop), foreground and background, plus received counts and latency p50/p95. Screenshots of anything unexpected.

title: v1.0 — tag the release
description: Gate: M5b done on both boards and the M6 runtime criteria met. Images attached to the release, docs/STATUS.md updated. See docs/PLAN.md gates out of M5b and M6.

title: M5b — Network validation on real hardware
description: Prove `internal/netmgr` on a Raspberry Pi 2 and a Cubieboard running a normal distro, and choose the WiFi dongle. Needs the boards and the dongle; blocks the runtime part of M6 and v1.0. Scenarios: docs/PLAN.md#m5b, results in docs/hardware.md.

title: M6 — Buildroot images: runtime validation
description: Build side is done (both images build and were inspected offline). What is left: boot the Pi 2 and BeagleBone Black images and check the runtime exit criteria — boot time, RAM, M5b scenarios on the images, 50 power cuts, watchdog.

title: M2 — Experiment: invisible coordination signals
description: Research milestone: can two binaries exchange signals inside a chat with nothing visible in any client? Output is a results document plus a decision for M3b, not product code. Needs two WhatsApp accounts on two phones (one Android, one iPhone) and the experiment switch `WAT_EXPERIMENTS=1`. Design: docs/PLAN.md#m2.

title: mDNS: send the unsolicited announcements on address change (M5 step 9)
description: PLAN.md M5 step 9 requires two unsolicited responses 1 s apart when an interface address changes. `mdns.Announce` (internal/netmgr/mdns/serve.go) implements exactly that and is unit-tested, but nothing calls it: `managed.serveMDNS` only answers queries via `mdns.Listen`, and nothing detects an address change. Effect: a client that resolved wa.local while the device was on the setup AP keeps the old IP until its 120 s TTL expires (queries for the new address still work). Wire it: remember the last address per interface in serveMDNS, call mdns.Announce on change, fake clock + table test in netmgr, and cover it in the M5b scenario that switches from AP to home WiFi.

title: Turn coordination claims on by default
description: Code is merged with claims off (`-coord-claims`). Once M2 says which variant is invisible, make it the default, update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (D-decisions on coordination) and docs/STATUS.md, and run the M3b field test: 20 notes from A, 20 from B, 20 from a third person → 0 duplicates / 0 missing, plus a run with B's instance stopped.

title: M2: experiment switch and probe sender/receiver (WAT_EXPERIMENTS=1)
description: No hardware needed. `internal/bot/experiment.go` + `internal/wa/experiment.go`: owner-only `!probe` sends V1–V6 ten seconds apart and logs `probe-tx variant=… id=…`; `wa.convert` logs `probe-rx variant=… field=… latency_ms=…` for reactions and the ContextInfo fields. Unreachable without the env switch so it can be deleted after the experiment.

title: M8: read the Italian replies in a real chat
description: Owner, needs a phone. Set language to Italian and go through `!help`, `!status`, `!transcription`, the `!t` hint, `!reset` and the password replies; report typos or awkward wording.

title: M7: run the image on an arm64 or armv7 host
description: Owner. Pull `ghcr.io/emdioh/wa-transcriber:v0.1.1` on a Pi or another arm host and repeat the amd64 checklist: setup page, pairing, one transcription, `!reset` re-exec, restart keeps the pairing.

title: M7 leftovers — arm host and package visibility
description: Everything else in M7 is done and verified on amd64. Remaining: run the published image on an arm64 or armv7 host, and optionally make the ghcr package public.

title: M7: make the ghcr package public
description: Optional; needs a token with `admin:packages` and the repository visibility decision. Documented in docs/STATUS.md as a known limitation meanwhile.

title: M6 build side: BR2_EXTERNAL tree and both images
description: Done. `os/` pinned to Buildroot 2024.02.9, `make -C os check`, images for Pi 2 and BBB build from a clean checkout and were inspected offline (partitions, init scripts, binary). 38.6 MB / 47.8 MB gzipped.

title: M8 leftover — Italian replies on a phone
description: Code and tests for the `it` reply language are done; nobody has read the Italian replies in a real chat yet.

title: M8: startup log of effective settings
description: Done. One line per start with provider, model, languages, listen address, data dir and memory limit, secrets redacted.

title: M8: reply language en/it with completeness test
description: Done. `config.Language`, `internal/bot/i18n.go` with a key per reply, `TestMessagesComplete`, language select on the System page.

title: M8: public_url on the Network page
description: Done. Shown when network management is off (Docker), validated as `http(s)://`; `!status` already printed it.

title: M7: verify the container end to end (amd64, Podman)
description: Done 2026-11-20: fresh volume owned by 65532, healthy probe, setup, real pairing surviving a restart, an OpenRouter transcription, `!reset` re-exec, root-owned legacy volume refused with the hint.

title: M7: Docker image hardening
description: Done. `scratch` image, uid 65532, `:8080`, tzdata built in, `HEALTHCHECK`, 24.5 MB on disk. Legacy root-owned volumes fail fast with the `chown` hint.

title: M7: release workflow
description: Done. Tags `v*` publish three binaries + `SHA256SUMS` and a multi-arch image on ghcr.io; `v0.1.0`/`v0.1.1` released, per-platform compressed sizes logged since `v0.1.1`.

title: M7: CI workflow
description: Done. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: gofmt check, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `make dist`, dist uploaded as artifact. Green on `main`.

title: M5 — Network manager (code)
description: Done as code. `internal/netmgr` with none + managed modes: ethernet, WiFi client, setup AP, mDNS `wa.local`, clock. Unit tests use scripted `Runner`/`FS` fakes; nothing has run on real hardware (that is M5b).

title: M7: /healthz endpoint and -healthcheck flag
description: Done. `GET /healthz` answers without a session (also while the setup AP runs) and `-healthcheck` exits 0/1; `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile uses it.

title: M4 — Web UI
description: Done. First-visit setup, sessions, System/Network/Status pages, pairing by QR and by phone number, `!status` showing the UI URLs.

title: M3b — Multi-transcriber coordination (code)
description: Done as code. `internal/coord` claims + watchdog, tagged transcription replies, claim/tag recognition in `wa.convert`, simulation tests with a fake bus. Claims stay off by default until M2 decides: a separate open task tracks turning them on.

title: M3 — Transcription and translation (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini)
description: Done. Settings resolution per chat, three providers, language detection, transcription queue, translation. OpenRouter verified with a real voice note inside the container (2026-11-20); translation and Gemini are covered by unit tests only.

title: M1 — WhatsApp skeleton
description: Done. whatsmeow client, QR pairing and unlinking, message filter, commands (`!status`, `!help`, `!password`, `!reset`, `!t`, `!transcription`), config store, RAM log buffer, Dockerfile. Verified on a real account: pairing/unlinking, automatic and on-demand transcription posted as a quoted reply.
